newsitem.title: USA: Koop, Kessler urge Congress to start over on tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Koop, Kessler urge Congress to start over on tobacco.

text.p: Leading tobacco critics C. Everett Koop and David Kessler urged a congressional panel Tuesday to start over in crafting a national tobacco control policy instead of trying to change what they called a "flawed" settlement negotiated by the industry and state officials.

Koop, a former U.S. Surgeon General, and Kessler, the former head of the Food and Drug Administration, made their strongest case yet against the proposed settlement. At a Senate Commerce Committee hearing, the two told lawmakers that they can "do better."
The two prominent physicians said Congress should craft a simple policy based on public health needs, not on terms that would keep "the industry booming and profitable."
"Take clear steps to reduce smoking in America without ceding an inch," Kessler said.

The two outlined six steps, including giving the FDA clear authority to regulate nicotine, banning cigarette advertising and marketing directed at children, punishing tobacco companies if youth smoking does not decline and banning smoking in all public places.
The panel is holding hearings on the complex settlement plan under which the tobacco companies would pay $368.5 billion but would get protection from certain types of lawsuits in the future.
